=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): whorled (multiple leaves are clearly attached at the same node, visible in multiple images, particularly in Image 1 and 5)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): clustered (leaves are grouped closely at nodes along the stem, as seen in all images)
B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (each leaf is a single, undivided blade with no leaflets)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): N/A
C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.)): entire (margins are smooth without teeth or serrations, visible in all images)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): elliptic (leaves are broadly oval with tapering ends, best seen in Image 2 and 5)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acute (tip is sharply pointed, as seen in Image 2 and 4)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): rounded (base is gently curved, visible in Image 1 and 5)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (main vein runs from base to apex with lateral veins branching off, visible in Image 2)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): visible, closely spaced, numerous (secondary veins are clearly visible and run parallel to each other, forming a dense network, as seen in Image 2)
    13. Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): shiny (surface is glossy and reflects light, evident in all images due to moisture)
    14. Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs on leaf surface; surface appears smooth)
    15. Petiole length (short / long): short (petioles are short, connecting leaf to stem, visible in Image 4 and 5)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (petioles are round in cross-section, no wings or grooves visible)
D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): woody (stem is brown, firm, and shows some bark texture, visible in Image 3 and 4)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs on stem surface)
    19. Stem color: brown (stem is light to medium brown, visible in Image 3 and 4)
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): ridged (stem surface has slight ridges and rough texture, visible in Image 3 and 4)
E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no stipules observed at leaf bases)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed (no exudate visible when stem or leaf is broken)
    23. Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent (no swollen joint at leaf base visible)
    24. Tendrils (present / absent): absent (no tendrils observed)
F. Notes: Some leaves show holes and margin damage, likely due to mechanical or biological factors, but cause is not determinable from images. The seedling appears to be growing in a moist, leaf-littered environment. Images show multiple views of the same individual, confirming whorled leaf arrangement and simple leaf morphology. Moisture on leaves suggests recent rain or high humidity.
